candidates.title: Ask HN: How does one build an LLM router with a labelled set of 100 tasks?
candidates.raw_content: I already spent the time building rubrics for a set of ~100 tasks on various criterias (accuracy, thoroughness communication style ). Then ran these on a few models and now have a labelled-set where I know for each task which is the cheapest/fastest model that gets a minimum threshold ( say 80 ). How does one go on to build a router based on this ? There appears to be no good literature / open source projects on this. I tried a bunch of approaches with the help of claude: - trying to use Jev via a serious of probe Yes/No questions ( does task contain x, does the world have y ...etc ). But this didn't yield good results. - kNN on embeddings of the task - in retrospect this was set to fail from the tasks, as now I think we do need some sort of NN to figure out the world/task complexity. - classifying prompt-complexity - something like https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/nemo/models/prompt-task-and-complexity-classifier/- The main issue from a conceptual standpoint is that one cannot fully predict how hard a task is until you are into the task - like you might encounter unknown nuances or issues in later stages, but classification has to happen at start. So I am starting to doubt if this is even possible tbh Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50575992 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

candidates.title: As these network attacks and impersonation attempts happen, who's securing the elderly? Especially thinking about my parents and grandparents. There are four layers I can think through where this could work. One is at the browser level, where somebody builds a secure browser that ensures that whatever websites they're going to are secured. Texts typically lead to a link, even for payments. This is why browser is key. Two could be at the network layer, where there is a physical device, similar to Pi-hole, or an Onavo-like VPN on your phone, that blocks websites that could be deemed unsafe. Three could be at the payments layer, where transactions that look like scams get flagged before the money leaves. And fourth and most crazy could be at the phone level, where everything is monitored, and you're only getting calls from your loved ones. Cloned voices would work with a provider like Reality Defender. There are individual solutions for this today but none neatly packaged. This could all be packaged with insurance that covers any activities on the OS or phone. In that way, incentives are aligned to keep this on the edge. The buyer would be the kids, someone like me, who get alerted when something looks off.
